target.title: fix(device-pair): bound notifier polling overlap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a slow device-pair notification poll could overlap later 10-second ticks and race notification state or send duplicate pairing reminders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notifier now keeps one service-lifetime poll in flight and skips interval ticks until it settles. The guard releases after success or failure, while initial polling, delivery behavior, cadence, and stop semantics remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive duplicate pairing notifications because one slow delivery crossed a polling interval, and polling resumes normally after the pending work settles.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/device-pair/notify.test.ts` on Node 24.18.0: 3 tests passed.
- Regression coverage advances multiple intervals while a poll is deferred, verifies stop/start does not overlap it, and proves polling resumes after both resolution and rejection.
- Scoped `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`: passed.
- `git diff upstream/main...HEAD --check`: passed.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.

## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled notifier lifecycle proof

- Base commit: `a5c5e3b713e7c16225394196af2cb37413f6fe22`.
- Exact PR head: `f8baa416e8fb70617042976cc70fdb1d6cf45e1e`.
- Scope: the committed regression test invokes the production `createPairingNotifierService().start()/stop()` lifecycle. It replaces only the device-pair listing boundary, uses the repository plugin-state test runtime, and drives the production 10-second interval with fake timers.
- Command:

  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/device-pair/notify.test.ts --reporter verbose
  ```

- Transcript:

  ```text
  RUN  v4.1.9
  PASS device-pair notify persistence > skips interval ticks while a notify poll is pending and resumes after it settles
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       3 passed (3)
  ```

- Observation: the production service made one initial poll and one interval poll. While that second poll remained pending, two more interval ticks and a stop/start cycle started no additional poll. After settlement, the next tick started one poll; two more ticks while that poll was pending again started none. Rejection released the guard, and the following tick resumed polling. The focused test also retained the existing subscriber persistence coverage.
- Not tested: live Telegram delivery, a real device-pair request, a full Gateway process, or wall-clock waiting. The remote pairing-list boundary is controlled and timers are simulated, so this proves notifier lifecycle and overlap behavior rather than external service behavior. Crabbox was unavailable in this environment; hosted exact-head CI provides the separate repository validation.
